name: AgeMem

paper.title: Agentic Memory: Learning Unified Long-Term and Short-Term Memory Management for Large Language Model Agents

construction.unit: LTM entry: free text the agent chooses to store, with an embedding, metadata and an id
construction.kept_as: agent-written text (whatever the policy puts in an Add_memory call)
construction.processing: no fixed extraction step: the policy decides in its own output whether to call Add / Update / Delete
construction.writer: the agent policy itself (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct or Qwen3-4B-Instruct, RL-trained)

organization.structure: flat long-term vector store + the agent's short-term context (message list)
organization.stores: LTM: in-memory vector store; STM: the running message context
organization.index: dense embeddings, cosine (text-embedding-v4, 256-d, in the released code)

management.operations: LTM: Add / Update / Delete by memory_id; STM: Summary (LLM rewrites a span as one message), Filter (drops messages similar to a criterion)
management.conflicts: the agent updates or deletes an entry whose id it saw in an earlier retrieval
management.forgetting: Delete tool (LTM); Filter removes context messages (STM)

retrieval.query: a query the agent writes in a Retrieve_memory call
retrieval.candidates: cosine similarity against every LTM entry (optional metadata filter)
retrieval.selection: top-k, k chosen by the agent (default 3; paper: typically 3-5)
retrieval.budget: 8,192-token context, 2,048-token responses; up to 5 rounds per stage (released config)

use.context: the agent's own context: system prompt with the six tool schemas, messages, and retrieved entries appended as tool messages
use.reasoning: multi-round think / tool call / answer loop by the same policy

classify.note: The trained agent decides whether to search, what query to write and k; the store then returns the k most similar entries by cosine, with no reranking.

stages.ingestion: Pre-task information arrives as ordinary messages in the agent's context; for HotpotQA the code sends all context paragraphs (up to 10 sentences each) as one 'casual chat' message.
stages.construction: The agent writes long-term entries itself by calling Add_memory with content, metadata and a type; each entry is embedded and stored with a new id.
stages.organization: One flat vector store of entries (content, embedding, metadata, id) plus the short-term message context; no links or hierarchy.
stages.update: Update_memory rewrites and re-embeds an entry, Delete_memory removes one (both need an id seen in a retrieval); Summary_context replaces a span of messages with an LLM summary and Filter_context drops messages judged similar to a criterion (threshold 0.6).
stages.retrieval: Retrieve_memory embeds an agent-written query and appends the top-k entries by cosine (k default 3) to the context as a tool message with their ids.
stages.answer: The same policy answers from its context after up to 5 think/tool rounds; there is no separate reader.
stages.learning: Three-stage rollouts (store from context; manage context under distractors after a context reset; answer the question) are scored once at the end, and step-wise GRPO gives every step of the trajectory the same group-normalised advantage (K = 8 rollouts). Trained on HotpotQA only.

summary: Memory operations on a vector store (add, update, delete, retrieve) and on the agent's own context (summarise, filter) become tool calls of the agent itself, trained end to end with a three-stage RL curriculum and step-wise GRPO.
notes:
AXES-CHECK: control is learned-rl at every stage because the RL-trained policy emits every memory tool call; the operations themselves are fixed code (cosine top-k) or an external Qwen-Max (Summary, Filter). Venue: the arXiv PDF (v3, 23 Jul 2026) names no venue; 'ACL 2026' comes from the authors' GitHub repo description ('ACL 2026 SAC Highlight'), and track 'main' is assumed from that label, not stated. Code: y1y5/AgeMem (owner matches the first author's handle, not linked from the PDF), pinned at 98f563f9 (2026-04-24). It covers only the HotpotQA workflow.
DESIGN: §3.1-3.5, §4.1, App. A.1-A.3, C.4; code train_hotpotQA.py, eval_hotpotQA.py, memory_store.py, agemem_train.yaml. Benchmarks are agent environments (ALFWorld, SciWorld, PDDL, BabyAI) plus HotpotQA, not long-dialogue memory benchmarks.

headline: Memory is not a pipeline around the model: the RL-trained agent itself decides when to store, update, delete, retrieve, summarise or filter.
Retrieval is plain cosine top-k over a flat store; what is learned is when to call it and what to store.
Summary and Filter are executed by an external Qwen-Max in the released code, not by the trained model.

open_questions: How is memory used on ALFWorld, SciWorld, PDDL and BabyAI? The paper says Stage 1 context comes from HotpotQA supporting facts and gives no pre-task context for the other four; the code has no workflow for them.
The HotpotQA evaluation skips the distractor stage, so the STM tools trained in Stage 2 are not what the HotpotQA score measures.

discussion.takeaway: Give an agent tools for both a long-term store and its own context and train when to use them with RL. Trained only on HotpotQA, AgeMem beats LangMem, A-Mem and Mem0 on average over five agent benchmarks in its own paper.

claims.claim: Unified, learned memory management beats memory-augmented baselines.
claims.evidence: Average 41.96 (Qwen2.5-7B) and 54.31 (Qwen3-4B) vs best baselines 37.14 (Mem0) and 45.74 (A-Mem). Table 2, §4.2

claims.claim: RL training is what makes the tools pay off.
The agent stores better long-term memories.
claims.evidence: Memory quality 0.533 and 0.605 vs 0.527 (Mem0) and 0.587 (A-Mem). Fig. 2

claims.claim: Learned context tools use fewer tokens than retrieval at every step.
claims.evidence: 2,117 vs 2,186 (−3.1%) and 2,191 vs 2,310 (−5.1%) prompt tokens on HotpotQA. Fig. 3

claims.claim: LTM tools, RL and STM tools each add accuracy.
Memory-aware reward terms help beyond the task reward.
claims.evidence: J 0.544 vs 0.509 and memory quality 0.533 vs 0.479 against an answer-only reward. Table 4

claims.claim: Gains are not only from adding STM tools and RL to an existing memory.
claims.evidence: LangMem, A-Mem and Mem0 with the same ST/RL additions average 41.56, 41.70 and 40.67 vs 43.69 for AgeMem on three benchmarks. Table 7, App. D.3

limits: The tool set is fixed; finer-grained control is left open.
The benchmarks are controlled; long real dialogues and real users are untested.
Training trajectories come only from HotpotQA.
reading: Only HotpotQA comes with pre-task context (its supporting facts). The paper does not say what the agent can store before the task on ALFWorld, SciWorld, PDDL or BabyAI, and the repo has no code for them, so how memory works on four of the five benchmarks is undocumented.
In the released HotpotQA evaluation the distractor stage is off and the context is wiped after Stage 1: the score measures storing and retrieving, not the distractor handling trained in Stage 2.

Summary, Filter, distractor generation and all judging call Qwen-Max through an API. The trained model makes the decisions, but the context operations depend on a larger external model, which the paper's point about avoiding auxiliary expert models does not mention.
The code's reward differs from the paper's: weights 0.5 / 0.2 / 0.15 / 0.15 with an extra tool-efficiency term instead of 1/3 each; Filter uses LLM-scored similarity instead of embedding cosine.
Token savings are small (3.1% and 5.1%) and every variant stays near 2.1-2.3k tokens under an 8,192-token budget, so context overflow is not what separates the configurations.
The per-bar gains in Fig. 4 (e.g. '+10.6') are percentage points, although the text calls them %.
Without RL the tools can hurt: AgeMem-noRL is below no memory on PDDL (8.87 vs 10.15) and BabyAI (46.34 vs 50.80) with Qwen2.5-7B.
Baselines run with default settings and untuned backbones, while AgeMem's backbone is RL-tuned on HotpotQA; Table 7 addresses this on three benchmarks only.

abstract.text: AgeMem treats both long-term memory and the agent's working context as things the agent manages itself through tools. It can add, update and delete entries in a long-term store and retrieve, summarise or filter what is in its context. A three-stage RL curriculum (store, handle distractors, answer) with a step-wise GRPO that passes the final reward to every step teaches it when to use each tool. Across ALFWorld, SciWorld, PDDL, BabyAI and HotpotQA, and two Qwen backbones, it outperforms LangMem, A-Mem and Mem0.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on arXiv.
